newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-YEBOAH RISKS WRATH OF CLUB FOR HIS COUNTRY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-YEBOAH RISKS WRATH OF CLUB FOR HIS COUNTRY.

text.p: Tony Yeboah is risking the wrath of his English club Leeds to lead Ghana's attack in their vital World Cup qualifying tie against Morocco on Sunday.
The 30-year-old striker drew criticism from his club chairman this week after leaving for Accra on Monday to play for his country despite missing Leeds' last premier league match through injury.
"I know I'm not 100 percent game fit but it is an very important game and Ghana need me," he told radio interviewers this week.
Ghana, who have the best record in African competition, have never qualified for the World Cup finals and the group five encounter against Morocco could well decide the group.

The match is one of 10 African qualifiers due to be played at the weekend, with the outcome of several matches sure to give clear indications of Africa's five representatives at the World Cup finals in France next year.

Yeboah, who has not played for Ghana since March, returns to the squad at an opportune time after an almost full-strength Ghana team were beaten 4-0 by Togo in a friendly on Sunday and had two players sent off.
"Both us and Morocco are the group favourites and we have to do well against them. I know Leeds are upset because I was out with a hamstring injury but I believe I'll be OK on Sunday," Yeboah said.
"I can't say whether I'll play the full 90 minutes but I've been training in the gym and I'm hoping to start the match."
Morocco go into the match in top-form after an impressive year in which they averaged almost three goals a game.
Sierra Leone host Gabon in Freetown on Saturday in the group's other match.
The home side have some doubt over the availability of key midfielder Lamine Conteh, who earlier this week refused to train after a pay dispute with the country's soccer federation.
Both Cameroon and Nigeria, who were at the last World Cup finals in the USA, can strengthen their positions with second successive victories.
Cameroon host Angola in Yaounde on Sunday in a group four match while Nigeria travel to Nairobi to meet Kenya in group one.
Zambia, who fired coach Rould Poulsen after their surprise defeat by Congo in November, host South Africa in Lusaka on Saturday in group three.

The Zambians are at full strength for a match they can ill afford to lose. South Africa will be without suspended defender Mark Fish and have dropped midfielder Doctor Khumalo who scored in their last meeting against Zambia in Lusaka in 1994.

Tunisia's home against Egypt in Tunis on Sunday could also dictate the outcome of their group. The Tunisians are having to come to terms with the death at the weekend of key defender Hedi Benrekhissa, who suffered a heart attack while playing for his club Esperance aginst visiting French team Lyon.
Liberia travel to Namibia in another group two match but are likely to be without captain and paymaster George Weah, injured playing for AC Milan in the Italian league last month.
Other matches on Sunday see Burkina Faso hosting Guinea in group one, Zaire home to neighbours Congo in group three and Togo away in Zimbabwe in group four.
